A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rex solver research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; relocated material can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation, editing and tri-alanine sampling experiments, plus appendix studies of inversion trajectories and interpolation.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds reconstruction-error measurements, component ablations and runtime profiling.

M1.justification: The Lawson/Princeps construction, reversible coupling, underlying ODE/SRK schemes and Brownian reconstruction procedure remain. Corrected appendix expressions reconcile inconsistencies with the existing construction; component-removal variants are introduced as ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CelebA-HQ generation, COCO text-conditioned generation, InstructPix2Pix editing, FRLL interpolation and tri-alanine sampling, with inversion also studied in both. The new precision and component studies reuse existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark comparisons retain DDIM, EDICT, BDIA, O-BELM and the molecular-sampling comparators. Both conditional BDIA settings remain in the numerical table. EDICT's editing failure and omission from the editing table were already reported in v3; the new reconstruction comparison uses existing image baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds controlled FP32/FP16 reconstruction evaluations at 10, 20 and 50 steps, latent/pixel MSE measurements, GPU-determinism controls and component-ablation protocols. Editing-budget reporting becomes inconsistent: v3 states 100 steps, whereas v4 Figure 9 specifies 50+50 and Appendix G.3 specifies 100+100. An actual rerun or budget change is not established.

E4.justification: v4 adds systematic precision and nondeterminism tests, ablates reversible coupling, exponential transformation and time reparameterization, and profiles Brownian Interval overhead (Appendices H.1, H.6 and H.7). The earlier latent-space failure and interpolation analyses remain in H.8–H.9.

E5.justification: Fixed/shared seeds and sample averages remain the reporting practice. v4 adds no multi-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing 1% rule for highlighting near-best table entries is retained.

E6.justification: Tables 4, 8 and 9 add reconstruction errors, profiling measurements and ablation outcomes. For example, FP32 Rex(Euler) latent MSE is reported as 3.77e-9 at 10 steps and 8.85e-10 at 50 steps. The original generation, editing and tri-alanine table values remain unchanged, as do the qualitative image panels.

T1.justification: v4 corrects Proposition C.1's time variable and integrating-factor algebra, along with backward-step and stage indices in Appendix C. For example, the integrating factor changes from beta_0/beta_T to beta_T/beta_t. The principal convergence and stability results persist; the rough-path and Brownian time-change material is relocated rather than newly proved.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions add an explicit near-machine-precision reconstruction claim. The empirical contribution shifts from outperforming prior inversion methods to remaining competitive on generation and editing. The central reversible-solver, convergence-order, adaptive-step and Boltzmann-sampling contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands explanations of finite-precision behavior, higher-order versus stochastic sampling, and component tradeoffs. Some new interpretations overstate the evidence: Section 4.3 calls LPIPS 0.140 to 0.107 roughly a twofold improvement over O-BELM, although the ratio is about 1.31. The earlier overflow and distorted-latent limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes v3's forward/backward Rex and ShARK code listings and supplies a project-code link instead. It adds Boltzmann code/data repository information, pretrained-checkpoint provenance, and editing details including CFG, inversion endpoint and adaptive tolerances. Most existing training, noise-schedule and hardware specifications remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds Tan et al.'s Amortized Sampling with Transferable Normalizing Flows for the Boltzmann codebase and makes attribution of the computational graph and SRK construction more explicit. The substantive comparison with prior reversible and diffusion solvers remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 broadly edits the prose, condenses the contribution list and substantially rewrites the empirical narrative. It reorganizes the appendices by moving rough-path and time-change material into B, removing the code appendix and consolidating results into H. These changes go beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main-text layout, restyles mathematical statements and substantially rearranges displays. It adds a reversibility schematic, reconstruction plot and new tables, while replacing prominent benchmark tables with radar charts and moving their numerical values to the appendix. Existing qualitative panels are retained and resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new reconstruction tests, component ablations and corrected Appendix C algebra improve empirical support and checkability. However, v4 introduces consequential inconsistencies: Figure 1 claims zero error regardless of precision despite Table 4's nonzero errors, Section 4.3 overstates the O-BELM editing improvement, and Figure 9 conflicts with Appendix G.3 on step budgets. These gains and losses affect central accuracy and reproducibility claims, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
